newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Three killed in Nigerian protest - reports.
newsitem.headline: Three killed in Nigerian protest - reports.

text.p: Three people died in a Nigerian communal protest in which scores of workers of the local unit of oil giant Royal Dutch/Shell have been held hostage, local newspapers reported on Wednesday.
They said the three were Ijaw tribesmen killed in protests on Tuesday in which the home of a prominent politician was burnt over the relocation of their local government headquarters.

Shell spokesmen in Lagos were not immediately available to comment. The company said on Tuesday that 31 of its Nigerian workers detained by villagers on six flow stations seized in the protest had been freed while 96 others were still being held.

The crisis which began last Saturday forced Shell to shut down operations in the six stations and forced it to cut back production by 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude, about five percent of Nigeria's total output of almost two million bpd.
But it said this was not affecting the volume of crude oil exports from Nigeria.
Nigerian newspapers said shops and other businesses hurriedly closed on Tuesday in the midwestern oil town of Warri, where Shell has its western Nigeria operational headquarters.
They said riot police were drafted in while the local military administrator Colonel David Dungs had summoned community leaders to a meeting to resolve the situation.
